_comment: ngsolve plasticity#4 (load stepping required for J2 + hardening; divergence signature). Observed 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604, plane-strain J2 on unit_square maxh 0.3 VectorH1 order 2, traction 500 with sigma_y 250 and H 100: one shot returns (-1, maxit) and prints 'Warning: Newton might not converge!' at maxit 30, 100 and 200 alike, so 'increase the steps, not maxit' is confirmed. But the returned pair is (status, numit) -- the claim's '(iters, conv) with iters == maxit' names them in the opposite order and expects an error value Newton never returns. Increments of 100% and 40% of sigma_y diverge; 20%, 10% and 5% converge to the same max|u_x|. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 raises N_STEPS_WRONG from 1 to 10, i.e. the one-shot traction is replaced by 20%-of-sigma_y load increments -- the guidance's own remedy ('reduce the load increment, not maxit'). Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 11 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'oneshot_first_element=-1', 'oneshot_diverged_at_every_maxit=True', 'oneshot_second_element_equals_maxit=True', 'raising_maxit_does_not_help=True' and makes the forbidden 'FAIL:' appear, so the fixture goes red. Note that 'Warning: Newton might not converge!' survives the mutation because the n=2 and n=5 coarse-increment runs in the right-variant section still diverge, so that expectation is not tied to the one-shot pathology. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
